# Rasterization Pipeline Optimization


## Overview
Rasterization Pipeline Optimization refers to techniques that accelerate the rendering of 3D Gaussians by improving the efficiency of the rasterization stage, addressing the bottleneck of processing non-intersecting pixels and managing memory bandwidth [S1]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by focusing on the computational pipeline (sorting, hardware acceleration, and culling) rather than the primitive representation or shading models.

## Shared principles
The family shares the goal of reducing the computational overhead associated with projecting and compositing 3D Gaussians onto a 2D image plane. Common mechanisms include:
1.  **Tile-based Processing:** Dividing the image into fixed-size tiles (e.g., 16x16 pixels) to localize Gaussian-pixel interactions [S2].
2.  **Depth Sorting:** Ordering Gaussians by depth within each tile to enable efficient front-to-back alpha compositing [S1, S2].
3.  **Culling:** Eliminating Gaussians that do not intersect with the view frustum or specific tiles to reduce the number of projected primitives [S1, S2].

## Subtopics

### [Speedy-Splat Rendering Pipeline](3543-speedy-splat-rendering-pipeline.md)
A GPU-accelerated rasterization method that replaces coarse bounding-box tile intersection tests with precise Gaussian-tile intersection checks and sorting-based depth ordering. It addresses the inefficiency of standard 3D-GS rasterization, which overestimates Gaussian extents and processes non-intersecting pixels, by generating a sparse set of Gaussian-tile pairs and sorting them for efficient pixel-wise compositing. See [Speedy-Splat Rendering Pipeline](3543-speedy-splat-rendering-pipeline.md).

### [Hardware-Accelerated Gaussian Rasterization](7329-hardware-accelerated-gaussian-rasterization.md)
A hardware-algorithm co-design that augments standard triangle rasterizers with dedicated units for Gaussian projection and blending, achieving an order of magnitude speedup in the rasterization stage. It solves the bottleneck of rendering 3D Gaussians on general-purpose GPUs by offloading specific computational patterns to specialized hardware pipelines. Unlike general-purpose compute shaders, this method isolates preprocessing and rendering into distinct hardware stages, optimizing data flow and reducing memory bandwidth requirements. See [Hardware-Accelerated Gaussian Rasterization](7329-hardware-accelerated-gaussian-rasterization.md).

### Single-Pass Color and Depth Rasterization
A rendering optimization where color and depth are rendered in a single rasterization process, reducing runtime compared to separate passes [S1].

## Background
The optimization of rasterization pipelines for Gaussian Splatting emerged as the method gained popularity for its real-time rendering capabilities. Standard rasterization approaches suffered from overestimation of Gaussian extents, leading to unnecessary computations for non-intersecting pixels [S1]. Subsequent works introduced precise intersection checks [S1] and hardware-specific optimizations to further improve performance [S2]. The method is primarily used in real-time 3D reconstruction and SLAM systems where high-fidelity rendering speed is critical [S1].
